R-01.title: Fast charging for hassle-free long trips
R-01.motive: Customers want to travel long distances without worrying about charging delays or network access.
R-01.attr: DC charging speed and charger network availability
R-01.target: The next model should enable a typical 20-80% DC charge in under 30 minutes at widely available public chargers, with seamless access to major charging networks.
R-01.accept: Product managers verify by test charging at multiple public DC stations and confirming both speed and network access meet expectations.
assume: Public DC chargers are available in key markets
Charging speed is not limited by software
Major charging networks are accessible without extra steps
R-01.cs: US G60 BEV owners report that 'long-distance charging is way too hard' and lack of a dedicated fast charging network is a major pain point (G60-0256); charging and range issues appear in 80% of pain comments for G60 BEV (F-011), and charging complaints are much higher for BEV (19.1%) than ICE (0.5%) (F-001).
R-01.conflict: There are only three explicit purchase reasons for charging in the comments, and no owner comments from China. Swedish owners mention improved AC charging but still note hassle on long journeys (G60-1910). Evidence is thin on DC charging experience outside the US, and current options do not list DC charging for G60.

R-02.title: Confident highway range for long trips
R-02.motive: Customers want to travel long distances without worrying about running out of range, especially at highway speeds or in winter.
R-02.attr: Usable electric range at highway speed and in cold weather
R-02.target: The vehicle delivers at least 80% of its WLTP range at 120 km/h in winter conditions, with clear in-car prediction and no unexpected drops.
R-02.accept: Product manager verifies by winter highway road tests and checks customer feedback for range complaints after launch.
assume: WLTP range is a known reference for customers
Highway and winter conditions are the main pain points
Range prediction is visible to the driver
R-02.cs: Customer comments (113 difficult to use, 43 defects, 2 purchase reasons, e.g. G60-3218, G60-3233) show range and charging are frequent pain points, especially for BEV owners.
R-02.conflict: Direct owner praise for real-world range is rare, and most feedback is negative or about charging difficulty (F-011, G60-3218). China has no owner comments and is only represented by study data. Purchase reasons for range are mentioned in just 2 comments, so positive evidence is thin.

R-03.title: Spacious and Luxurious Rear Seat Experience
R-03.motive: Customers want their passengers to enjoy exceptional comfort and space in the rear seats, making every journey feel premium.
R-03.attr: Rear seat legroom, comfort, and amenities
R-03.target: The successor must provide rear seat space and comfort that consistently scores above 8.5/10 in customer studies across all major markets, with clear passenger praise for legroom and amenities.
R-03.accept: Product managers verify the target by reviewing customer study scores and analyzing owner comments for positive mentions of rear seat comfort and space.
assume: Customer studies accurately reflect real-world comfort
Rear seat amenities are maintained or improved
No major packaging changes reduce rear space
R-03.cs: BMW customer comments (G70-2573, G60-2215, F70-0652) praise rear seat comfort and roominess, with 19 likes and 8 wants out of 54 total comments.
R-03.conflict: There are no direct purchase reasons or conquest comments for rear seat lounge, and evidence from China is modelled from studies, not owner comments. Some complaints exist about entry comfort (G70-2574, F70-0764), and the evidence is thinner for F70 and G60 compared to G70.

R-04.title: Effortless Control of Car Functions
R-04.motive: Customers want to quickly and easily access features without distraction or frustration.
R-04.attr: Menu structure and intuitiveness of controls
R-04.target: Any primary function should be accessible in two taps or less, and 90% of users should rate the system as easy to use in post-delivery surveys.
R-04.accept: Verify by customer studies showing at least 8/10 ease-of-use scores and by usability tests confirming two-tap access for main features.
assume: Survey items reflect real-world digital UX
Two-tap access covers most-used functions
Voice and screen interactions are included
R-04.cs: BMW customer comments show 613 complaints about difficult-to-use digital features, with only 6 citing digital UX as a purchase reason (R-04).
R-04.conflict: Evidence is strong for complaints about complexity and unintuitive menus (613 'difficult to use' comments, R-04), but positive comments about digital UX are rare as explicit purchase drivers (only 6, R-04). China has no owner comments and is modelled from the study. Some praise the system as 'mostly straightforward to learn' (G60-0415), but others find 'the whole apps setup feels clumsy' (F70-1070) or 'using the tech isn't very intuitive' (F70-1689).

R-05.title: Intuitive controls for distraction-free driving
R-05.motive: Customers want to operate core functions easily and safely without taking their eyes off the road.
R-05.attr: Ease of reading and using physical controls
R-05.target: Successor must achieve at least 8.4/10 for 'easy to read and use instruments/controls/displays' in EU and CN customer studies, and at least 5.2/7 for 'placement/ease of reading and using controls' in the US.
R-05.accept: Product manager verifies by matching or exceeding these study scores in post-launch customer research.
assume: Study items accurately reflect customer experience with physical controls
Physical controls remain available for core functions
Market-specific needs are addressed
R-05.cs: Customer comments show 75 complaints about difficult-to-use controls and only 1 explicit purchase reason (R-05).
R-05.conflict: Evidence is thin on explicit purchase reasons for physical controls, with only 1 comment (R-05). China has no owner comments and is modelled from the study. Some US feedback highlights frustration with digital alternatives (G60-3645), supporting the need for intuitive physical controls.

R-06.title: Reliable software and seamless connectivity
R-06.motive: Customers want their vehicle's digital features to work consistently and without frustration.
R-06.attr: Stability and reliability of digital services
R-06.target: The next model must achieve a customer-rated reliability score of at least 9.0/10 in EU and 8.5/10 in CN for software and connected services, and reduce defect and difficult-to-use complaints by 30% compared to current models.
R-06.accept: Product managers verify the target by analyzing post-launch owner surveys and tracking the volume of software-related complaints in the first 12 months.
assume: Customer study scores reflect real-world experience
Complaint volume is a valid indicator of reliability
OTA updates are included in digital services
R-06.cs: BMW customer comments show 281 defect and 214 difficult-to-use complaints related to digital experience (R-06), with specific issues like malfunctioning navigation (G60-1677), ConnectedDrive services (F70-1826), and remote engine start failures (G70-0810).
R-06.conflict: Evidence is strong in EU and US, but China has no owner comments and is modelled from the study. Some positive comments about digital features exist (G70-1295), but negative feedback and complaints are much more frequent. There is no evidence on over-the-air updates specifically.

R-07.title: Trusted hands-off driving on highways
R-07.motive: Customers want to feel safer and more relaxed during long highway drives by relying on advanced driver assistance.
R-07.attr: Hands-off highway driving with reliable lane and speed control
R-07.target: The system must enable hands-off driving on highways for at least 15 minutes without disengagement or driver intervention under normal conditions.
R-07.accept: Product manager verifies by test-driving on highways and confirming uninterrupted hands-off operation for 15 minutes, and by reviewing customer feedback for trust and ease of use.
assume: Highway assistant is available and legal in target markets
Customers are informed about system capabilities and limitations
R-07.cs: Customer comments include requests for highway assistant functionality (G70-3664) and show 3 explicit purchase reasons, but also 161 complaints about difficulty of use and 81 defect reports.
R-07.conflict: Evidence is strong for customer interest and safety as a motive, but owner comments are almost exclusively from the US and do not provide detailed praise for hands-off operation. There are significant complaints about usability and defects, indicating the current experience may not fully meet expectations (G70-3664, R-07). China is only represented by study data, not owner comments.

R-08.title: Conversational Assistant Needs to Be Easier
R-08.motive: Customers want a digital assistant that is intuitive and reliably understands their commands.
R-08.attr: Ease of use and voice recognition accuracy
R-08.target: The personal assistant should achieve at least a 5.5/7 satisfaction score for voice recognition performance in the US customer study.
R-08.accept: Verify the next model's US customer study shows a voice recognition score of 5.5 or higher.
assume: Study methodology and scale remain consistent
Voice assistant is available in all tested vehicles
R-08.cs: No customer comments cite the personal assistant as a purchase reason (0/121), but 61 report it is difficult to use (e.g. G60-3645, G60-0415).
R-08.conflict: There is thin evidence for the personal assistant as a purchase driver, with no owner comments from China and no direct purchase reasons in any market. Most feedback relates to usability issues rather than positive motivation.

R-09.title: Premium materials and quiet cabin feel
R-09.motive: Customers want a luxurious, comfortable environment that feels high quality and refined.
R-09.attr: Perceived interior material quality and cabin quietness
R-09.target: Successor models must achieve at least 8.5/10 for 'quality of interior and materials used' and 7.5/10 for 'quietness when driving' in EU and CN customer studies, and at least 5.7/7 for both 'quality of interior materials' and 'freedom from wind and road noise' in US studies.
R-09.accept: Product manager verifies by reviewing customer study scores and monitoring owner feedback for praise or complaints on interior quality and cabin noise.
assume: Customer study methodology remains consistent
Scores reflect real customer perceptions
No major market-specific issues arise
R-09.cs: BMW customer comments (640 total, 374 likes, 109 wants) show frequent praise for 'very high quality, both in materials and in how they are put together' (G60-2254), but also some requests for more leather and lighting customization (G60-0229) and occasional noise complaints.
R-09.conflict: Evidence is strong in EU and US, but China has no owner comments and is modelled from the study. Some complaints about noise and requests for more premium touches exist, but positive feedback on quality dominates (G60-2254, G60-0229).

R-10.title: Exterior design that turns heads
R-10.motive: Customers want a car that stands out and makes them feel proud of its appearance.
R-10.target: At least 80% of surveyed owners rate exterior styling 9/10 or higher in EU and 5.7/7 or higher in US.
R-10.accept: Product manager verifies target by reviewing owner survey scores and comparing them to the set thresholds.
assume: Survey methodology remains consistent across generations
Styling changes are visible and relevant to customers
R-10.cs: BMW customer comments show 13 likes for exterior design in the G60 (e.g. G60-1232, G60-0490), with customers stating they 'really like the design' and 'appreciate the overall style'.
R-10.conflict: Evidence is thin in China, as there are no owner comments and only study data is available. Some US comments mention the vehicle size as 'not user friendly' (G60-3852), but this does not directly address design identity.

R-11.title: Agile, Enjoyable Handling and Ride
R-11.motive: Customers want a car that is fun to drive and feels confident on the road.
R-11.attr: Driving dynamics: agility, steering feel, ride comfort, power delivery
R-11.target: The successor must score at least 8.0/10 for 'handling' and 'ride' in EU and CN customer studies, and at least 6.0/7 in the US, with positive owner comments outnumbering complaints by at least 3:1.
R-11.accept: Product manager reviews customer study scores and verifies owner comment ratios in each market after launch.
assume: Study items and comment classifications remain consistent
Driving dynamics are not compromised by new technologies
Market sample sizes are sufficient for reliable ratios
R-11.cs: Owner comments show strong praise for handling and ride (F70-0650, F70-0651, F70-1340, G60-0671, G60-0228), with 5 purchase reasons and 302 wants on driving dynamics.
R-11.conflict: China has no owner comments and is modelled from the study. Some US complaints mention difficult-to-use features, but direct negative feedback on driving dynamics is rare (F-008).

R-12.title: Transparent and Controllable Data Settings
R-12.motive: Customers want to feel confident that their personal data is handled securely and that they have clear control over what is shared.
R-12.attr: User control over data sharing and privacy settings
R-12.target: The successor must provide a clear, user-friendly interface for managing data privacy settings, allowing customers to easily view, adjust, and understand what data is collected and how it is used.
R-12.accept: A product manager verifies the target by testing the data privacy interface with real users, ensuring they can locate and adjust privacy settings without assistance and understand the implications of their choices.
assume: Customers value transparency and control over their data
Data privacy settings are accessible in the vehicle or companion app
R-12.cs: No BMW customer comments directly mention data privacy, transparency, or control (0 of 39, all models, R-12).
R-12.conflict: Evidence is thin: there are no customer comments or study findings on data privacy, transparency, or local processing for this cockpit. The topic is modelled only from the study definition and German option lists, with no direct owner feedback from any market (R-12).

R-13.title: Easy, Reliable Hands-Free Access
R-13.motive: Customers want to load and unload their car quickly and easily, especially when their hands are full.
R-13.attr: Hands-free tailgate and comfort access reliability
R-13.target: The hands-free tailgate and comfort access system must work on the first try at least 95 percent of the time in customer hands.
R-13.accept: Product manager verifies by field testing and monitoring customer complaints about failed or difficult access in the first six months after launch.
assume: Customers value ease of entry and trunk operation
Hands-free features are available on key models
Customer complaints reflect real-world usability
R-13.cs: Customer comments show 287 'difficult to use' and 162 'defect' complaints (e.g. G60-3647), but only 1 explicit purchase reason.
R-13.conflict: Evidence is strong for usability problems and defects, but explicit purchase motivation is rare (only 1 comment). China has no owner comments and is modelled from the study. Some complaints refer to partial trunk opening (G60-3647), indicating reliability issues.

R-14.title: Seats that stay comfortable on long drives
R-14.motive: Customers want seats that remain supportive and comfortable for extended journeys, enhancing overall driving enjoyment and reducing fatigue.
R-14.target: Successor seats must achieve at least 8.8/10 in EU and 5.9/7 in US customer comfort studies, with positive comments on seat comfort outnumbering negative ones by at least 2:1.
R-14.accept: Product manager reviews customer study scores and verifies that positive seat comfort comments (e.g. 'especially comfy seats', F70-0652) are at least double the negatives in owner feedback.
assume: Customer studies remain comparable in methodology
Owner comment volume is sufficient for robust ratios
R-14.cs: BMW customer comments show 65 praise mentions for seat comfort (e.g. F70-0652, G70-2573) and only 4 purchase reasons, with 194 difficult-to-use and 127 defect mentions (R-14).
R-14.conflict: Evidence is strong for seat comfort in EU and US, but China has no owner comments and is only represented by study scores. Purchase reasons are rare in comments (4/649), so emotional motives are mostly inferred from praise and study data.

R-15.title: Seamless smartphone integration and connectivity
R-15.motive: Customers want their phones to connect easily and reliably for music, apps, and digital keys, making daily use more convenient and familiar.
R-15.attr: Ease and reliability of phone pairing and features
R-15.target: The next model must allow users to pair their phone, use CarPlay/Android Auto, charge wirelessly, and access digital key features without connection drops or confusing steps.
R-15.accept: Product manager verifies by user testing: pairing, charging, and app features work first time and remain stable for at least 30 days in 95% of cases.
assume: Wireless charging and smartphone integration remain standard
Digital key and app features are supported for major phone brands
R-15.cs: Customer comments show 74 wants, 265 difficult to use, and 114 defect reports (e.g. G60-3648, G70-0771, G60-1020) about phone integration, with only 2 citing it as a purchase reason.
R-15.conflict: Evidence is strong for usability pain and defects, but very thin for explicit purchase motivation (only 2 comments). China has no owner comments and is modelled from the study. Some US study scores for mirroring and charging are below average (G60, G70).

R-16.title: Practical storage for daily essentials
R-16.motive: Customers want enough space for luggage and small items to support daily routines and travel.
R-16.target: The successor must achieve at least 8/10 satisfaction for both interior storage and luggage capacity in EU and CN customer studies, and 5.5/7 in the US.
R-16.accept: Product manager reviews customer study scores and confirms they meet or exceed the target values in all major markets.
assume: Customer study methodology remains consistent
Storage features are comparable across generations
R-16.cs: Customer comments include 2 purchase reasons, 162 complaints about difficulty of use, and 52 defect reports related to space and storage (e.g. F70-0266, G70-3783).
R-16.conflict: China has no owner comments and is modelled from the study. Some comments mention insufficient storage or smaller luggage compartments (F70-0266, G70-3783), but positive purchase reasons are rare. Evidence is strong in volume but thin on explicit purchase motivation.

R-17.title: Control over automatic start-stop function
R-17.motive: Customers want to decide when the engine start-stop activates for a smoother and more predictable driving experience.
R-17.target: The successor must offer a clear and accessible way for drivers to disable or override the automatic engine start-stop function at will.
R-17.accept: Product manager verifies that customers can easily find and use a manual override for start-stop, confirmed by positive owner feedback and absence of complaints about lack of control.
assume: Customers value direct control over start-stop
Override is clearly labeled and accessible
System remembers driver preference
R-17.cs: US customers (1 want, G60-1676) miss the override button for auto start-stop and workaround by using sport mode; no positive comments about the current solution.
R-17.conflict: There are no purchase reason comments or positive feedback for the current smart start-stop implementation. Evidence is thin, with only one clear complaint (G60-1676) and no China owner comments or German option data.

R-18.title: Sound system that impresses passengers
R-18.motive: Customers want a premium audio experience that matches the luxury feel of their BMW and impresses both themselves and their passengers.
R-18.target: At least 80% of owners rate the sound system 6 or 7 out of 7 for overall performance in post-purchase surveys.
R-18.accept: Verify the target by reviewing post-purchase survey results and checking that at least 80% of respondents rate the sound system 6 or 7.
assume: Survey scale and methodology remain consistent
Sound system options are clearly communicated to customers
R-18.cs: Only 2 purchase reason comments mention premium audio, but 80 likes and 40 rival comparisons show strong interest (R-18).
R-18.conflict: Customer comments rarely mention premium audio as a direct purchase reason (2/291), but survey data shows high satisfaction scores (G60: 5.5/7, G70: 5.11/7). China has no owner comments and is modelled from the study.

R-19.title: Stress-free parking with camera support
R-19.motive: Customers want to park easily and confidently, especially in tight spaces or complex environments.
R-19.attr: Assisted parking with visual camera guidance
R-19.target: The system enables drivers to park in standard parking spaces without stress or confusion, using clear camera views and automated assistance.
R-19.accept: Product manager verifies by observing customer use in real parking scenarios and checking for confusion or complaints about the parking assistant and camera features.
assume: Camera and assistant features are available and activated
Customers use the system in typical parking situations
R-19.cs: Customer comments show 112 complaints about difficulty of use and 48 defect reports for parking and cameras, but no explicit purchase reasons (R-19, G70-2120).
R-19.conflict: There are no customer comments from China and no explicit statements that parking assistant or cameras are a purchase driver. Evidence is thin on positive experiences or direct purchase motivation, with most feedback focused on defects or usability issues (R-19, G70-2120).

R-20.title: Easy, Reliable Climate Comfort for All Seats
R-20.motive: Customers want a climate system that is simple to use and keeps everyone comfortable in any weather.
R-20.target: Successor must provide intuitive controls and consistent comfort for all passengers, with at least 90% positive feedback on usability and effectiveness in customer studies.
R-20.accept: Product manager reviews customer study scores and owner comments for complaints about climate control usability or comfort, aiming for less than 10% negative feedback.
assume: Customer feedback remains a reliable indicator of usability
Multi-zone systems are standard or widely chosen
Study scales and comment classifications remain consistent
R-20.cs: Customer comments show 224 complaints about difficult-to-use climate controls and 88 defect reports (R-20), with specific mentions of air conditioning not running when ignition is off (G70-3783) and requests for easier air conditioning settings (G70-2898).
R-20.conflict: Evidence is strong for usability pain points, but positive comments or clear purchase drivers are rare (only 1 purchase reason in 352 comments, R-20). China has no owner comments and is modelled from study scores. Some comments mention defects but not direct purchase motivation.

R-21.title: Standard features that match expectations
R-21.motive: Customers want to feel they are getting good value for the price paid.
R-21.attr: Level of standard equipment versus rivals
R-21.target: The successor offers all key features that customers expect as standard, matching or exceeding direct competitors in standard equipment.
R-21.accept: Product manager verifies by benchmarking standard equipment lists against main rivals and confirming customer study scores improve by at least 0.5 points.
assume: Competitors' standard equipment is known and up to date
Customer expectations are stable year-on-year
R-21.cs: Several customers (e.g. F70-0232, F70-0272) comment that basic features are optional extras and expect more standard equipment for the price.
R-21.conflict: Evidence is strong for the UK and EU, but there are no owner comments from China and only study data for that market. Some praise the car's value (F70-2018), but others feel it 'feels a bit basic for what it costs' (F70-0272), showing mixed perceptions.
